claims.claim_text: Two postwar radio-industry sources document a Leon H. Baumlin with wartime Navy radioman service; the uncommon-name candidate may be the indexed person, but no direct OSS linkage has been established.
claims.evidence_excerpt: I joined the Navy in '43—saw service as a Radioman 1st Class
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A 1947 trade journal identifies Leon H. Baumlin as a wartime Navy radioman working in commercial radio, and a 1962 RCA publication documents the same exact name as a radiotelegraph operator.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable only. The exact full name is uncommon and the wartime communications background is compatible, but the index supplies no rank, identifier, birthplace, or assignment with which to confirm the match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Navy service began in 1943; the commercial-radio and RCA evidence is postwar and is not evidence of a pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: No employer claim is created. Box 43 remains necessary to test whether the indexed Leon H. Baumlin is the Navy radioman and to establish any pre-OSS chronology.

claims.claim_text: The indexed George W. Bauserman is confirmed as the Army enlistee represented by the exact-name record in the official merged enlistment file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and private service identifier match across the OSS index and official Army enlistment file; the full identifier is not public.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an exact full-name and unique private-identifier match, with enlisted Army service compatible across the records.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official record dates Army entry to 26 April 1943; the index establishes later OSS personnel-file inclusion but supplies no assignment date.
claims.match_notes: The decisive identifier is retained only in the private database and masked in the public interface and exports.

claims.claim_text: At Army entry on 26 April 1943, George W. Bauserman's record carried civilian occupation code 138, a group covering motorcycle mechanic, high-explosives packer, toolroom keeper, stock clerk, or stock-control clerk.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official file supplies code 138 and the entry date; the secondary code table expands it to several occupations but does not identify which one applied or name an employer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact name and matching private identifier across the index and official Army file.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to Army entry on 26 April 1943. It may describe pre-service work, but it is not proven to be the immediate pre-OSS occupation.
claims.match_notes: The complete occupation group is shown without selecting one occupation or inferring an employer.

claims.claim_text: The private identifier printed for Vito L. Bavosa conflicts with the official Army merged file, where it belongs to John J. Hanning; no exact Vito L. Bavosa row was found in that file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A private-identifier lookup in the official Army file resolves the index-carried number to a different name. An exact-name search found no Vito L. Bavosa row, and a different Vito A. Bavosa record carries a different identifier.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Conflicting. The index row itself is preserved, but the printed identifier cannot safely be used to resolve Vito L. Bavosa to an Army enlistment record.
claims.temporal_assessment: No reliable pre-OSS chronology can be derived until the Box 43 personnel file or another direct record resolves the discrepancy.
claims.match_notes: The full identifier is retained only in the private source record and excluded from public data. Neither John J. Hanning's history nor Vito A. Bavosa's history is attributed to this person.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Ting Bawm is high-confidence matched to Havildar Bawm Ting, the Kachin Burma Rifles soldier recruited in the field by SOE in 1944.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Havildar Bawm Ting: Born in 1911, Bawm Ting was a Kachin
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare two-part name appears in reversed order under Kachin naming practice, and the archival-research biography supplies a distinctive Burma Rifles and SOE wartime context consistent with the OSS index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the rare name pair, plausible name-order reversal, Kachin identity, Burma Rifles service, and direct SOE wartime context. The Box 43 file is still needed for a direct American OSS linkage.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source dates Burma Rifles entry to 8 January 1933 and SOE field recruitment to 1 January 1944; the date and nature of his OSS-index relationship remain unresolved.
claims.match_notes: The site preserves the indexed form Ting Bawm and records Bawm Ting as a documented variant; it does not claim that every SOE assignment was an OSS assignment.

claims.claim_text: Bawm Ting served in the 2nd Battalion, Burma Rifles from 1933 and held the rank of Havildar before SOE recruited him in the field on 1 January 1944.
claims.evidence_excerpt: joined the Burma Rifles on 8 January 1933, serving with 2 Burif
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The source explicitly sequences a long Burma Rifles assignment before SOE field recruitment and records the promotions to Lance Naik, Naik, and Havildar.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match based on the rare name pair and the Kachin, Burma Rifles, and SOE context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate before SOE recruitment, but the timing and nature of the person's American OSS-index relationship are unknown; therefore the site does not label it immediate pre-OSS.
claims.match_notes: This is a military assignment, not a civilian employer. The Box 43 file should establish whether the OSS record reflects liaison, assignment, or another relationship.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Belgian lieutenant Andre Bayet is high-confidence matched to André Bayet, alias BOVY, the Belgian SOE officer who entered SOE on 19 October 1943.
claims.evidence_excerpt: André Bayet fut parachuté le 7 mai en tant que lieutenant ARA
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional biography matches the exact name, Belgian nationality, lieutenant status, and Allied special-operations context; it dates SOE entry and two wartime missions.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence because exact name, Belgian note, lieutenant rank, and SOE wartime context all align. The Box 43 file remains necessary to establish the precise OSS relationship.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source dates SOE entry to 19 October 1943 and missions in 1944-1945 but gives no civilian or military affiliation immediately before SOE or OSS.
claims.match_notes: The wartime post-office engagement described under mission cover is not treated as civilian employment. No pre-OSS employer claim is created.
